stimulus.text: Paraphrase of accounts of the Great Society's critics and its legacy. The programs cost a great deal, and some critics said they burdened taxpayers and fostered a culture of dependency among the people they were meant to help. Others on the left said the programs did too little and left poverty and racial injustice in place. The poverty rate fell by about 40 percent during the Johnson years, yet poverty did not end. Medicare and Medicaid remained in place, a legacy that endured into the twenty-first century.

stem: Which judgment about the Great Society is best supported by the whole passage?

options.text: It failed completely, leaving nothing behind
options.misconception: Medicare and Medicaid remained in place into the twenty-first century, so something was left behind.

options.text: It ended poverty and racial injustice for good
options.misconception: The passage says poverty did not end and critics on the left said racial injustice remained.

options.text: Partial success: poverty fell, programs endured, goals unmet
It changed nothing about American life
options.misconception: The poverty rate fell by about 40 percent and two major programs endured, so it changed a great deal.

rationales.A: Medicare and Medicaid remained in place into the twenty-first century, so something was left behind.
rationales.B: The passage says poverty did not end and critics on the left said racial injustice remained.
rationales.C: The poverty rate fell by about 40 percent and Medicare and Medicaid endured, yet poverty did not end.
rationales.D: The poverty rate fell by about 40 percent and two major programs endured, so it changed a great deal.
rationales.general:
1. The passage gives a success: the poverty rate fell by about 40 percent.
2. It gives a second success: Medicare and Medicaid endured into the twenty-first century.
3. It also gives the limit: poverty did not end, and racial injustice remained.
4. The fair judgment is therefore partial success, not triumph or failure.
Remember: Weigh the gains and the limits together before judging.
